title: SSH Returns Permission Denied (publickey)
symptom: SSH connection reaches the EC2 instance but fails authentication with: 'ec2-user@203.0.113.10: Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)'.
initial_observations: SSH debug output shows client offering private key, but server rejects it.
environment: EC2 Linux instance running Ubuntu or Amazon Linux.

possible_causes.cause: Wrong default AMI username used (e.g. using ec2-user on Ubuntu or ubuntu on Amazon Linux)
possible_causes.evidence_needed: AMI platform check vs SSH connection username.
possible_causes.remediation: Connect with the standard username for the AMI: ec2-user for AL2/AL2023, ubuntu for Ubuntu, admin for Debian, centos for CentOS.

possible_causes.cause: Local private key file permissions too open on client machine
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Client SSH warning: 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE! Permissions 0644 are too open'.
possible_causes.remediation: Restrict private key permissions: chmod 400 key.pem (Linux/macOS) or icacls reset/grant on Windows.

possible_causes.cause: Wrong private key used (does not match public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys)
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Fingerprint mismatch between local private key and KeyName assigned in EC2 launch config.
possible_causes.remediation: Specify the matching private key corresponding to the KeyPairName displayed in EC2 console.

investigation_steps.title: Run SSH in Verbose Mode (-v)
investigation_steps.explanation: Inspect the authentication handshake and identify which identity files are offered.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Check 'Authentications that can continue' and reason for key rejection.

investigation_steps.title: Verify Instance AMI Platform and Assigned Key Pair Name
investigation_steps.explanation: Confirm the official AMI OS type to deduce default username, and verify the KeyName.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Check KeyName matches the private key file you are using.

investigation_steps.title: Check Local Private Key File Permissions
investigation_steps.explanation: OpenSSH clients refuse keys with permissions wider than 0400 or 0600.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Ensure file is readable only by the owner.

verification: Execute `ssh -i mykey.pem <correct-user>@<public-ip>` and confirm interactive shell prompt opens.
prevention: Adopt AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to eliminate reliance on SSH key pair files.
Enforce standardized AMI naming and key management via AWS Secrets Manager.
